statement: For an n × n square matrix A with complex entries, the determinant det(A) is a scalar-valued function of its entries equal to the product of its eigenvalues: \det(A) = \prod_{i=1}^{n} \lambda_i = \lambda_1 \lambda_2 \cdots \lambda_n.

symbols.meaning: i-th eigenvalue of A (counted with algebraic multiplicity)

properties.property: A matrix A is invertible if and only if \det(A) \neq 0
properties.why: \det(A) = 0 if and only if 0 is an eigenvalue of A

properties.property: \det(\exp(A)) = \exp(\operatorname{tr}(A)), and for any logarithm L such that \exp(L) = A, \det(A) = \exp(\operatorname{tr}(L))
properties.why: every eigenvalue \lambda of A corresponds to eigenvalue \exp(\lambda) of \exp(A)

properties.property: \det \begin{pmatrix} A & B \\ C & D \end{pmatrix} = \det(D) \det(A - BD^{-1}C) when D is invertible
properties.why: factoring the 2x2 block matrix using the Schur complement

properties.property: \det(I_m + AB) = \det(I_n + BA) for m x n matrix A and n x m matrix B (Sylvester's determinant theorem)
properties.why: forming square matrices of size m x m and n x n respectively

properties.property: \chi_A(t) = \det(t \cdot I - A) defines the characteristic polynomial, whose roots are the eigenvalues of A
properties.why: eigenvalues \lambda are precisely the values satisfying \chi_A(\lambda) = 0

properties.property: \operatorname{tr}(I - A^{-1}) \leq \log \det(A) \leq \operatorname{tr}(A - I) for positive definite matrix A
properties.why: derived via the Kullback–Leibler divergence between two multivariate normal distributions

assumptions.breaks_when: The matrix has dimensions m x n with m != n

assumptions.assumption: Matrix entries are defined over the complex or real numbers
assumptions.breaks_when: Matrix entries belong to an algebraic structure where standard eigenvalue decomposition or arithmetic operations are undefined

failure_modes.cause: Zero is an eigenvalue of A, indicating the matrix is non-invertible
Matrix has dimension m x n where m != n
